question: How can documents represented as real-valued tf-idf vectors be classified by Rocchio and kNN, how do these relate to linear and nonlinear classifiers, and how does the bias-variance tradeoff guide method choice?
hypothesis: Contiguity hypothesis: documents in the same class form a contiguous region and regions of different classes do not overlap.
contributions: kNN classification with time complexity and 1NN error bound
Linear versus nonlinear classifiers; Rocchio and NB as linear

limits: No experiments or datasets: all numbers are worked examples on a five-document toy set (Table 13.1/14.1), a hand-made linear classifier (Table 14.4) or a confusion matrix adapted from Picca et al. (2006) with no stated classifier.
Only Euclidean distance and cosine variants of Rocchio/kNN covered; chapter text does not give accuracy of kNN or Rocchio on any benchmark and defers to Chapter 15 Table 15.2.
Authors concede that treating 'linear' as weak and 'nonlinear' as strong in the bias-variance discussion is a simplification (p.308-309); the decomposition is for MSE of P(c|d) not for 0/1 error.

Approximate fast kNN is said not to be tested for text: 'it is not clear whether they can achieve much better efficiency than Theta(|D|) without a significant loss of accuracy' (p.300). Dated: 2008 sparse tf-idf vectors; no dense embeddings, ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF, product quantisation) or learned retrieval; only Andoni et al. (2006) LSH and Kleinberg (1997) cited.
Curse of dimensionality for nearest-neighbour distances is not discussed; the claim that linear separability becomes likelier with dimension is left as an exercise.
Text of the book mentions choosing k and b' by tuning but gives no values or procedure beyond held-out selection.
practices: Use length-normalized tf-idf weights for vector space classification; unweighted and unnormalized counts should not be used (p.290).
Use Rocchio only when classes are roughly spherical with similar radii; use kNN for non-spherical, multimodal or disconnected classes if the training set is large (p.290, 296).
For two-class Rocchio use a modified rule with a positive offset b (or just distance to the positive centroid below b') to avoid false positives (p.296).
Prefer odd k to avoid ties; k=3 or 5 typical, 50-100 sometimes; or select k on held-out training data (p.298).
Weight kNN votes by cosine similarity, which is often more accurate than plain voting (p.299).
For kNN preprocess training documents once at training time; consider an inverted index for sparse documents (p.299-300).
If a problem is linear use a simple linear classifier; if nonlinear, nonlinear classifiers are often more accurate (p.305).
For any-of tasks build one classifier per class (class vs complement) and apply independently; for one-of tasks assign to the class with max score, confidence or probability (p.306-307).
Use the confusion matrix to target feature work at the largest error pairs (p.307-308).
Weigh bias against variance when choosing a learning method; there is no universally optimal method (p.308, 312).
Tune k and b', and engineer and select features, because Rocchio and kNN effectiveness depends heavily on them (p.315).

terms.definition: Documents in the same class form a contiguous region and regions of different classes do not overlap.
Classification by distance to class centroids, centroid = vector average of members (Eq 14.1).
Assign the majority class of the k nearest neighbours; decision boundary determined locally.
Decomposes space into cells, each of all points closer to one object than to others.
kNN memorises all training examples and compares the test document to them; also instance-based learning.
The average error rate of classifiers learned by a method for a particular problem.
A two-class classifier that decides class membership by comparing a linear combination of the features to a threshold.
Existence of a hyperplane that perfectly separates the two classes.
A document that, when included in the training set, misleads the learning method and increases classification error.
Classes not mutually exclusive; a document can be in several, one or none; J independent classifiers.
Classes mutually exclusive; each document belongs to exactly one; also multiclass, single-label.
For each pair of classes, how many documents from c1 were incorrectly assigned to c2.
Squared difference between P(c|d) and the prediction of the learned classifier, averaged over training sets (Eq 14.12).
Average squared difference between the prediction and its average over training sets (Eq 14.13).
The learning method also learns from noise, which increases MSE.
A class consisting of several clusters that are not close, e.g. Burma/Myanmar before and after 1989.
